newsitem.title: EGYPT: Volume perks up but prices slip on Cairo bourse.
newsitem.headline: Volume perks up but prices slip on Cairo bourse.

text.p: Trade on the Cairo stock exchange perked up but share prices slipped on Monday, partly from profit-taking by foreign investors, brokers said.

Mills, cement and real estate shares again grabbed the top three rankings in terms of turnover, which snowballed overall across the board to hit 107.3 million pounds ($31.6 million), compared to Sunday's low 48.5 million pounds.
The index was down a sober 1.36 points to 394.14 points, the Capital Market Authority (CMA) said.
"Compared to yesterday there was a lot of volume," said Fabienne Gimenez of brokers EFG Hermes. "I think the market will remain stable for the next couple of weeks."
"There is profit-taking from new foreign investors. But it's a healthy market and there is a lot of supply and demand. The retail people are supporting the market," she said.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills saw the most action with 5.77 million pounds turnover. Its shares fell 0.50 pounds to close at 106 pounds.
Medinet Nasr Housing and Development was again the most active housing firm, with shares worth 5.46 million pounds changing hands. It ended down 4.00 pounds at 494.
Helwan Portland Cement, the most active share of the day on Sunday, fell 0.14 pounds to close at 79.01. Its turnover of 4.8 million pounds put it third.
"Regarding the cement sector these are some of the most liquid shares in the market," Gimenez said.
Other mills also went down for the second day. East Delta Flour Mills lost 0.66 pounds to 84.89, and Upper Egypt Flour Mills 3.00 to close at 88 pounds.
"Foreign investors are selling a part of their portfolio and taking profit," Gimenez said.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 631.42 from 640.85 points on Sunday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms was down at 266.76 points from 267.22.
Out of the 88 shares traded, 23 gained, 39 lost and 26 ended the day unchanged.
